title: Spectral proof of Friendship Theorem via Mathlib linear algebra

problemStatement.formal: ∀ G : SimpleGraph V, IsFriendshipGraph G → Fintype.card V ≥ 3 → ∃ c, IsUniversalVertex G c
problemStatement.plain: In any finite simple graph where every pair of distinct vertices has exactly one common neighbor, there exists a vertex adjacent to all other vertices. This is proved using spectral methods: the adjacency matrix equation A² = (k-1)I + J leads to eigenvalue constraints that force the existence of a universal vertex.
whyMatters: Fundamental result in extremal graph theory
Connects spectral graph theory to structural results
The spectral proof technique (A² analysis) is broadly applicable

proven: UCN extraction and uniqueness (ucn, ucn_spec, ucn_unique)
A² off-diagonal identity: |N(u) ∩ N(v)| = 1 for u ≠ v
Counting identity partition: disjoint fibers, full cover, n-1 = Σ(deg(v)-1)

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: FriendshipTheoremOQ01.lean has 0 sorries, 1 axiom. Full combinatorial infrastructure proved: UCN extraction/uniqueness, A² off-diagonal identity, counting partition (disjoint+cover+identity), regular constraint n=k(k-1)+1, number theory s|s²+1→s=1, regular→triangle→universal. New: separation lemma (neighborhoods of adjacent vertices are separated), partner involution (ucn is involutive on N(u)). The single axiom 'spectral_regular_friendship' captures eigenvalue analysis: k-regular friendship with k≥2 → k=2.
builtItems: ucn, ucn_spec, ucn_adj_left, ucn_adj_right, ucn_unique (proved) in FriendshipTheoremOQ01.lean
ucn_ne_left, ucn_ne_right (proved) - UCN distinctness from endpoints
friendship_separation (proved) - For adj u,v: ucn(x,v) = u for all x ∈ N(u)\{v}
ucn_involutive (proved) - ucn(u, ucn(u,v)) = v for v ∈ N(u)
ucn_unique_in_neighborhood (proved) - partner is unique neighbor within N(u)
insights: A² = (k-1)I + J is the heart of the spectral proof - each entry counts common neighbors
Separation lemma: for adj u,v, ucn(x,v) = u for ALL x ∈ N(u)\{v} — neighborhoods are fully separated
Partner involution: v ↦ ucn(u,v) is a fixed-point-free involution on N(u), implying deg(u) is always even
The counting identity uses an explicit partition V\{u} = ⊔_{v∈N(u)} (N(v)\{u}) with disjoint fibers
Adjacent vertices do NOT always have same degree (windmill counterexample: deg(center)=4, deg(petal)=2)
'No universal → regular' inherently requires spectral/algebraic methods — no clean combinatorial proof exists
Eigenvalue integrality is the deepest part: requires spectral decomposition of A²=(k-1)I+J
mathlibGaps: No ready-to-use spectral decomposition for real symmetric matrices in convenient graph theory form
adjMatrix squared connection to common neighbors not directly available as a lemma
No built-in all-ones matrix definition in Mathlib
